title: 1965 AHSME Problem 32
statement: An article costing \(C\) dollars is sold for \(\$100\) at a loss of \(x\) percent of the selling price. It is then resold at a profit of \(x\) percent of the new selling price \(S'.\) If the difference between \(S'\) and \(C\) is \(1\dfrac19\) dollars, then \(x\) is:

solutions.text:
A loss of \(x\%\) of the \(\$100\) selling price means \(C=100+x.\) On resale, \(S'-100=(\frac{x}{100})S',\) so \(S'=\frac{10000}{100-x}.\) Therefore \[ \begin{gathered} \frac{10000}{100-x}-(100+x)\\ =\frac{x^2}{100-x} =\frac{10}{9}. \end{gathered} \] Thus \(9x^2+10x-1000=0,\) whose positive root is \(x=10.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
